newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end mixed, eye on U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end mixed, eye on U.S. rates.

text.p: Chilean shares closed narrowly mixed in light turnover with investors staying on the sidelines as they wait to see if the Federal Reserve raises U.S. interest rates at its meeting on May 20, said traders.
The market is seen continuing sluggish for the next few days, with concerns the Fed may jack up rates dominating the bolsa, said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
"The bourse is dead. I don't see much changing until May 20 when we see what the Fed does," said Hurd.
The 40-share index closed up 0.11 percent at 118.82 points.
The general index lost 0.02 percent to 5,334.46 points in turnover of 8.5 billion pesos.

The market's mood was also dampened by fears the Central Bank may not cut interest rates again this year after comments from Bank president Carlos Massad that the economy may pick up in the second half of the year, said dealers.
"Some analysts had been speculating on a rate cut in May, but now some are questioning whether there will be a rate cut at all," said one dealer.
Winners included telecom CTC on hopes that U.S. carrier SBC Communications will not block the merger planned with VTR and will agree to sell its 40 percent stake in VTR, said traders.
CTC ended up 1.25 percent at 3,250 pesos.
Other gainers included banking stocks with Santander up 1.85 percent at 27.5 pesos and Santiago rising 1.1 percent to 9-1/5 pesos.
Declines included forestry firm Masisa, down 4.02 percent at 215 pesos and pension fund manager Provida which shed 2.04 percent at 7,200 pesos.
